title: Freeze the correspondence before the holdout
question: How much apparent correspondence arises from selecting among four correlated semantic scoring rules, and does that selection survive an independent balanced holdout?
model: Exact uniform distribution over 2520 permutations of balanced target labels. Four cyclic scoring matrices use 2 for an exact shifted label, 1 for either adjacent cyclic label, 0 for the opposite. Reports are fixed. The best discovery mapping is frozen before a fresh independent holdout.
incomingEvidence: B1 demonstrated prior and common-reporter ambiguity despite high scores. Balancing targets removes that particular advantage; B2 tests remaining flexibility in how correspondence is scored. The Pauli event-window example motivates fixed scoring/window boundaries but supplies no statistical evidence for this model.
limits: Finite cyclic labels are a methodology toy, not an embedding model or measured human synchronicity.
Zero live model calls and zero human observations.
The null targets and holdout independence are imposed by construction.
The proposed positive H-MEANING hypothesis requires an independently frozen dictionary/window and reproducible held-out excess; unrestricted retrospective interpretation is nonidentifying.
Discrete tests may be conservative; parameters are not tuned to force nominal-alpha exceedance.
The known-map positive control is inserted ordinary correspondence, not higher-source contact.
finding: Selecting a correspondence rule increases discovery scores and rejection relative to the fixed rule. Exact maximum calibration controls the declared finite null; a frozen discovery mapping returns to the null mean on independent holdout.
controls: Retrospective maximum with naive fixed-rule tail
Independent holdout with discovery mapping frozen
